interest: Shows 1941 Japanese police pressuring withdrawing American firms into generous severance payouts for local staff.
overview: Despatch (1941): Consul Warner reports a Kobe shipping firm's closure, with Japanese police mediating a severance deal after pressuring American firms into generous payouts.

people.name: Robert McClelland
people.role: Manager of the Kobe branch of the States Steamship Company

subfiles.about: Report on the settlement of retirement allowance disputes for Japanese staff of the States Steamship Company in Kobe and the manager's recommendation to close the office.
subfiles.summary: Warner reports States Steamship Co.'s Kobe branch closing, with police-mediated severance of one month's pay per year of service, part of a pattern of police-enforced payouts to dismissed staff.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Gerald Warner (Kobe) on Settlement of Retirement Allowance Difficulties of the States Steamship Company
